before: The aim isn't to stop enjoying pleasure or praise, though, and the same goes for gain and belonging. It's noticing when one of them has turned into a condition for having a self. Maybe some part of you is sure that if you lost it, there wouldn't be much of you left.
after:
Day to day, differentiation looks something like this:
- Other people's emotions and opinions stop automatically replacing your own. Their reasons can still change your mind, though.
- Noticing when you agreed in the moment and disagree later: "Wait, why was I nodding along?"
- Caring about somebody's feelings without sacrificing your own ground.
- Disappointing people and withstanding social pressure, and still being recognizably yourself wherever you are (maybe louder in some places). That one can take a while.
- Questioning what you were programmed to believe while holding the discomfort, and without having to stop loving anyone over it.

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Differentiation can happen inside family, religion, community, or relationship. Selective belonging still leaves room to belong. A differentiated adult can remain deeply embedded while retaining the freedom to question, disagree, or leave when staying would require disappearing. Families with individuated members are healthier than enmeshed families; autonomous faith is healthier than religious compliance; relationships between differentiated people are sturdier than mutual absorption.
brief:
- differentiation can happen inside a family, religion, community or relationship
- belonging selectively still leaves room to belong
- a differentiated adult can stay deeply embedded and still be free to question, disagree, or leave when staying would mean disappearing
- all three comparisons, each within its kind: families whose members get to be their own people (individuated) are healthier than enmeshed families; faith that's your own (autonomous) is healthier than religious compliance; relationships between differentiated people are sturdier than mutual absorption. Not "religion is unhealthy" or "closeness is bad"
- context, not for the text: temporary or permanent distance comes later in this h3, so leaving is said here once, briefly; danger doesn't wait for any of this ("get safe first", Also Look Outward)
